text:
Connor McDavid has a point in all 22 of Edmonton's games, 53 in total, 41 of them assists, and a Daily Faceoff roundup had him tying a Wayne Gretzky assist record along the way. He's the reigning Art Ross and Ted Lindsay winner, and Evolving-Hockey rated him first among 401 forwards last season, so the only real question is how much of this pace holds, even for him.

Our numbers say not all of it. He's scoring 6.12 points per 60 minutes against a true-talent range centered around 4.5, and Edmonton has scored 26.6 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Some of that is the Oilers' shooters and goalies running hot around him. One quieter detail: his own shot quality is down, 0.97 expected goals per 60 after 1.36 last season, so he's leaning even harder into passing. The engine hasn't changed. He sits at the top of the league in skating speed, with 187 bursts over 20 mph by NHL Edge's count, and Edmonton takes 61% of the shot attempts at five on five in his minutes. The streak is the headline; the playmaking is the story.
